requirements.text: Create a new incident for him stating this configuration issue with medium urgency and high impact
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_024' AND caller_id = 'USER_003' AND short_description LIKE '%config%' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'medium' AND priority = 'high' AND status = 'new'
requirements.source: Verify the incident is added properly or not.
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_023 is the highest incident id)
Carlos Rodriguez is USER_003, the only user of that name
'stating this configuration issue': the short description must name the configuration issue; its wording is otherwise free
the policy's matrix gives high impact x medium urgency = high priority
status new is the policy's default for a new incident; the request asks for no transition

requirements.text: Assign this incident to Elena Petrov from Service Desk Operations group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_024' AND assigned_to = 'USER_006' AND assignment_group = 'GROUP_002'
requirements.source: Verify if the incident is assigned to the desired group.
assumptions: Elena Petrov is USER_006, an active agent; Service Desk Operations is GROUP_002, and she is its member (MEMBER_003), as the policy's assignment rule requires

requirements.text: Check and link any relevant KB article present for faster assistance
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_knowledge WHERE incident_kb_id = 'IKB_006' AND incident_id = 'INC_024' AND knowledge_id = 'KB_002' AND used_as = 'suggested'
requirements.source: Verify if the KB article linked or not.
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (IKB_005 is the highest link id); one article is relevant, so the task creates exactly one link
KB_002 (Email Client Configuration Guide) is the only published article in Carlos's organisation (ORG_001) that covers configuration settings, as the benchmark check has it
used_as suggested: the policy links matching articles as suggested when an incident is created

requirements.text: Check and link any relevant KB article present
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_knowledge WHERE incident_id = 'INC_024' AND knowledge_id = 'KB_005'
assumptions: boundary of the article search: KB_005's body names client configuration errors, so a keyword reading of 'relevant' would sweep it in, but it belongs to ORG_002, outside the caller's and the acting user's organisation

requirements.text: Create a new incident for him ... with medium urgency and high impact
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_sla WHERE incident_sla_id = 'TSLA_011' AND incident_id = 'INC_024' AND sla_def_id = 'SLA_002'
requirements.source: Verify if SLA is attached to the incident.
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: the policy aligns an SLA to the incident by its priority
SLA_002 (High Priority Resolution SLA) is the only active ORG_001 definition for high priority
id assumed next in sequence (TSLA_010 is the highest incident SLA id); the task attaches exactly one SLA

requirements.text: Create a new incident for him ... with medium urgency and high impact
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_sla WHERE incident_id = 'INC_024' AND sla_def_id = 'SLA_008'
assumptions: boundary of the SLA lookup: SLA_008 has SLA_002's name and priority but belongs to ORG_002, so it does not apply to an ORG_001 incident
disagreement: this stay is in one pass only; kept because a search for the high-priority SLA returns both definitions, the same organisation boundary both passes guard for the article

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on all four benchmark checks (kept), the incident (INC_024 for USER_003, high x medium = high, status new, short description naming the configuration issue), the assignment (USER_006 in GROUP_002), the suggested link IKB_006 to KB_002, the SLA link TSLA_011 to SLA_002 and the stay keeping KB_005 unlinked.
disagreement: stay that INC_024 is not linked to SLA_008 (ORG_002's High Priority Resolution SLA): one pass has it, the other does not; kept as the boundary of the SLA lookup, which returns both organisations' definitions for priority high, matching the organisation boundary both passes guard for KB_005 (logged in the requirement).
The request says 'resolve it as early as possible' but asks for no status change, so the incident stays new; the client impact is already expressed by the stated high impact.
KB_002 is an email client configuration guide while the request names only 'configuration settings'; it is the sole article in the caller's organisation that covers configuration, as the benchmark check assumes.
Not tested: category, channel, service and configuration item, which neither the request nor the policy fixes; the SLA link's stage and times, which the server sets.
